crime: {WITCH_NAME}'s fourth foster mother stood behind her at the hall mirror, hands on her shoulders. "You fit right in here." She was sent back within the month.

In the prison, a girl who had learned the trade in her aunt's salon cut the prisoners' hair every evening at the tall mirror in the shower room, the only mirror in the prison. Whenever the hairdresser reached for {WITCH_NAME}'s hair, she stepped into the glass.

At seven one evening, the hairdresser held her shoulders from behind at the mirror. "You fit right in here. Tomorrow I'm cutting your hair." {WITCH_NAME} stepped into the glass out of her hands, and the girls waiting in line watched her go.

At seven-twenty, as the last of them left, the hairdresser turned on every hot shower to rinse the cut hair from the tiles, and the mirror fogged white. At seven-thirty she toweled a wide band clear so {WITCH_NAME} could come out. She came out through it, behind the hairdresser's turned back, took up the cutting cape laid out for her own haircut, twisted it around the girl's neck and held on until she was still. Then she wiped the misting band and stepped back into the glass. Steam whitened it behind her.
At seven-fifty a prisoner found the hairdresser dead on the tiles, the showers running, the mirror white. Only at eight-twenty, as the glass cleared, did {WITCH_NAME} step out in front of everyone.

In the trial court, the prisoners ruled that she had been sealed behind the fog. Fogged glass is no door; someone must have come in by the real one. Then a prisoner looked at the mirror once it had dried and saw a wiped band, with drip trails running down through the haze the steam had left. The prisoners realized the fog had been wiped open while the showers ran. {WITCH_NAME} had stepped out and strangled the hairdresser.
fields.epitaph: She never understood that the hand clearing the glass was asking her to stay.
fields.epithet: The Girl Whose Only Home Was the Glass
execution: On the execution stand, four tall mirrors swing shut around her, glass facing outward, and lock into a sealed pillar. Their silvered backs press against her shoulders and palms; on her side there is no glass at all. The spectators look at the pillar and see themselves in every pane, the whole court and not her. From behind the glass comes a knocking. It slows, then stops, and the pillar is silent.

magic.name: Behind the Glass
magic.text: She steps through mirrors into a silent, reversed copy of the world, empty of everyone else.
